subject: Aureus Dedicated Capacity — provisioning & regional fallback plan
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Liam Carter <liam.carter@aureus.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Aureus Dedicated Capacity — provisioning & regional fallback plan

Thanks again for the conversation this morning, Liam — good alignment on traffic patterns and the need for predictable baseline capacity with short daily bursts. Per our call I attached a short mutual action plan and a lightweight implementation checklist to get us moving. High-level asks from Redwood to confirm so we can size the pool and lock-in regional capacity: 

- Primary region preference (we'll need at least one active + one fallback).
- Preferred GPU family (A100 80GB vs H100) for initial provisioning and for staging perf tests.
- Expected steady-state concurrency / qps and expected peak burst multiplier + typical burst windows.
- Any compliance/KMS/BYOK constraints (we'll need KMS key alias if BYOK).
- Network requirements (IP allowlist, proxy, private endpoints).

Proposed defaults (we can change based on your answers):
- Primary region: us-west-2, fallback: us-east-1
- Baseline pool: 8 x A100-80GB nodes (min pool size 2 nodes for HA), autoscale min=2, target utilization 60%
- Burst policy: allow up to 2.5x additional nodes for scheduled 2–4 hour nightly windows; pre-warm KV cache during scheduled burst windows.
- Cutover / acceptance target: 2028-09-06 weekend maintenance window (tentative)

Next steps: please reply with the bullets above; Marissa/Monica will draft the onboarding timeline and a short runbook once we have region/GPU decisions. I attached: Aureus_Mutual_Action_Plan_v1.pdf and a checklist CSV with required accounts and network entries.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30 minute kickoff once the team confirms region/GPU.

--
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference
From: Liam Carter <liam.carter@aureus.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 14 Aug 2028 11:05:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Aureus Dedicated Capacity — provisioning & regional fallback plan

Rishi — thanks, this is great. Quick answers to your bullets (we synced internally):

- Primary region: us-west-2 (we prefer west for lower latency to our users), fallback: us-east-1.
- GPU: prefer A100-80GB for production; happy to run H100 in staging if you think it's helpful for performance tuning.
- Traffic profile: ~250 concurrent inference sessions at baseline. Expected steady-state throughput ~1,000–1,500 requests/min (we size by requests rather than tokens). Typical burst multiplier: ~2.5x for ~3 hours nightly (UTC 02:00–05:00 our local off-peak), and occasional daytime spikes up to 2x for <30 minutes.
- Compliance: SOC 2 Type II is required; BYOK/KMS is mandatory — we will provide a KMS key alias once you confirm the onboarding account. Data retention: 30 days logs/metrics.
- Network: our NetOps will provide an IP range and a list of endpoints; we require TLS mutual auth for any private endpoint and port 443.

Attached is our internal NetOps contact card (see platform@aureus.ai). Let's schedule the kickoff: Thu 16 Aug 10:00–10:30 PT works for us.

Subject: Re: Aureus Dedicated Capacity — provisioning & regional fallback plan

Appreciate the quick turn, Liam — answers look straightforward and we can proceed with the defaults you confirmed. A few clarifications and operational notes so the onboarding team can size and author the runbook: 

1) Autoscale policy and min/max: we'll set autoscale min=2 nodes, desired steady-state=8 nodes, and max for normal autoscale=20 nodes. The nightly scheduled burst will reserve an additional 12 nodes (which yields ~2.5x on your baseline) that we will pre-warm. If you want a hard cap lower than 20 let us know.

2) Pre-warming and cache: for fast ramp during the scheduled 3-hour burst, we'll pre-warm the KV and prefix cache 15 minutes prior. If you have a canonical prompt set, please share so we can include it in the smoke tests.

3) Fallback routing: primary region us-west-2, fallback us-east-1. We'll implement smart routing with sticky session affinity during region failover to avoid split KV states; there will be an automatic fallback policy in the routing table that routes only new requests to the fallback region and drains existing sessions. We'll include a cold-start mitigation doc in the runbook.

4) KMS/BYOK: share key alias and an IAM principal that Redwood should be granted to use the key. If you need HSM integrations, flag that now.

5) Acceptance tests: basic smoke (hello world), perf (95th p99 latency <500ms under steady load), functional regression tests on your top-20 prompts (please share).

Marissa — can you pick this up and propose a 6–8 week onboarding timeline (staging perf, security attestations, production cutover) and drop the checklist CSV into the shared onboarding doc? Monica/Hannah, please note netops contact in message thread for IP allowlist.

I'll block Thu 16 Aug 10:00 PT for a kickoff; Marissa, feel free to move if you want a different cadence.

--
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Aureus onboarding checklist and timeline (draft)

Hi team — draft checklist and recommended timeline below. Attached: redwood-implementation-checklist.csv (fields for NetOps, KMS, account invites).

Week 0 (prep) — Network & Access
- Receive IP allowlist and VPN/peering details from Aureus NetOps
- BYOK KMS alias + IAM principal provided and validated
- Invite Aureus service accounts to Redwood Console (read-only for initial validation)

Week 1–2 (staging & perf)
- Provision staging pool (2 x H100) in us-west-2 for perf testing
- Run perf suite with top-20 prompts; iterate quant/threads as needed
- Validate autoscale triggers: GPU util target 60% and scale step size 2 nodes

Week 3–4 (security & compliance)
- SOC 2 artifact collection and attestation (Redwood provides SOC 2 report + evidence links)
- Retention and logging confirmation (30 day metrics/log retention)

Week 5–6 (production provisioning & cutover)
- Provision production A100 pool (8 baseline nodes, autoscale up to 20), configure scheduled burst reservation + pre-warm hooks
- Run acceptance tests (smoke, perf, functional)
- Plan cutover for weekend (proposed 2028-09-06) with evening maintenance window

Operational notes:
- We will include a rollback plan that drains traffic back to hosted API if any regression occurs.
- For hotspot bursts, we'll pre-warm using a prioritized prompt list to minimize cold-starts.

Action items for Aureus: share prompt set (top-20), NetOps IP ranges, KMS key alias, and confirm maintenance window preference.

Thanks — happy to adjust timelines once you confirm the prompt set and netops contacts.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
